summary: A note from UCSB describing two commands, Login and Logout, for its Simple Minded File System, which let a user identify themselves and name an account for billing. It restates and completes RFC 399, adding a description of the responses these commands produce. It is a local service description, not a general standard.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 431 defines login and logout commands for UCSB's Simple Minded File System. Login identifies the user and account, while logout ends that association without closing the connection.

subtitle: Login and logout commands for UCSB's Simple Minded File System.

tldr.problem: UCSB's Simple Minded File System needed commands to identify a user and the account associated with file use; RFC 399's description was incomplete.
tldr.mechanism: LGI supplies a user name and account number, while LGO ends that association. Each command receives an eight-bit completion code.
tldr.outcome: RFC 431 restates and completes RFC 399 and updates RFC 122; it describes a local UCSB service.

sections.title: A Fuller Version of RFC 399
sections.content:
RFC 431 replaces RFC 399, which introduced login and logout commands for UCSB's Simple Minded File System (SMFS) but did not fully describe their responses. This RFC restates the commands and specifies the completion codes.

It also updates RFC 122.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier note introduced two commands but left out their replies. This document gives the fuller description.

sections.title: Login with LGI
sections.content:
The Login command, LGI, identifies the user and the account number to associate with SMFS use. It should be sent after the Initial Connection Protocol and before a command that refers to a file.

The user name and account stay in effect until another LGI, an LGO, or connection closure. At the time of the RFC, SMFS use was not billed, so the command was optional and the account number arbitrary.

LGI uses op code 13. Its user-name field may be at most eight characters, and its account-number field at most four; both use the filename character set.
sections.plainLanguage: LGI identifies a user and an account before file commands are sent. In the situation described by this RFC, login was optional because SMFS use was not billed.

sections.title: Logout and Completion Codes
sections.content:
Logout, LGO, ends the association between the user and the accounting information from the last LGI. It does not close the connection; LGO's op code is 14.

Each command's only response is an eight-bit completion code. On success the code equals the command's op code; codes 47 through 54 identify errors such as empty or invalid user-name and account fields, or an invalid user or account.
sections.plainLanguage: LGO ends the login association but leaves the connection open. The reply is a number that identifies success or a specific error.
